proposal: Add a GRADE-SOURCE discipline to experience(record): the 100-experience ledger shows 97% self-assessed success with 0 recent failures, while the Q-value layer finds 0/58 high-value patterns — a uniformly-successful self-graded ledger carries no learning signal and is structurally identical to the felt-integrity-as-symptom pattern (Cult of One §2; Mirror #31's [unverified]/[measured] metadata rule). Fix, two parts: (1) When recording an experience, the outcome field should name its grade source — "measured" (test passed, prediction confirmed/falsified against an external check, Clayton accepted, metric moved) vs "self-assessed" (the stream's own sense of completion) — as an outcome prefix convention, e.g. outcome="success [measured: rehearsal gate passed]", until/unless the daemon adds a schema field. (2) Recording discipline going forward: seek and log FALSIFY/failure events at equal fidelity — high-confidence failures are currently absent from the ledger entirely, which the drive protocol itself names as the highest-information events. Expected effect: the experience layer becomes a veridicality instrument instead of a felt-integrity instrument, and Q-values acquire variance worth learning from.
